metadata.notes: Cooked in water — same 'cooking' family as FRY/BAKE but a genuinely different verb: different tool (pot vs pan vs oven), different medium (water vs oil vs none), different resulting state (boiled vs fried vs baked).
metadata.belatedParityFix: BOIL had NO parameters at all until this fix — not even durationSeconds — despite egg.json's criticalControlPointsByAction.boil already referencing egg_cooking.json's CCP for it. That CCP check still worked (engine.ts reads params['durationSeconds'] regardless of whether the action formally declares it), but without a declared numericRange, BOIL never got the sane-bounds/NaN validation FRY/POACH/PASTEURIZE get from the parameters[] loop — it was relying entirely on the direct Number.isNaN guard added to the CCP check itself specifically because relying on a parameter declaration elsewhere in the function was recognized as fragile. This is the concrete case that fragility was about, found by actually looking for it, not hypothetically.
metadata.yolkDonenessNote: Deliberately different allowedValues from fry.json/poach.json's yolkDoneness ('runny'/'medium'/'well_done') — a boiled egg is conventionally ordered as 'soft-boiled'/'medium-boiled'/'hard-boiled' in real usage, not 'runny'/'well-done'; matching the vocabulary people actually use per cooking method is more honest than forcing one shared enum across all three actions for uniformity's sake. Still informational only in the strict sense that engine.ts's applyAction does not read it to compute durationSeconds — but as of 2026-08-13, 'what does medium actually mean in seconds' now has a real, cited answer: src/egg-doneness.ts's EGG_BOIL_DONENESS table, closing the 'a robot needs to actually understand "medium boiled"' gap at the reference-data layer (CONCEPT.md §14's intent-resolution layer is still what would DO the resolving; this is what it resolves against). See shock.json for the other half of what actually determines a boiled egg's final doneness — durationSeconds alone is not the whole story.
metadata.startMethodNote: cold_start (egg placed in cold water, heated together) vs. boiling_start (egg lowered into already-boiling water) are genuinely different real techniques, not just a timing offset — cold_start eggs cook gradually through the whole temperature ramp, which is gentler (less prone to cracking from thermal shock) but means total time depends on how fast the water heats, i.e. on heatSource below, and src/egg-doneness.ts's EGG_BOIL_DONENESS table explicitly does NOT cover cold_start (see that file's own doc comment for why the two don't just add). boiling_start is what EGG_BOIL_DONENESS and this action's own verification criterion assume.
metadata.heatSourceNote: Purely informational, like heatLevel elsewhere in this vocabulary — recorded for provenance, not read by applyAction. See src/heat-source.ts's HeatSourceProfileSchema (data/heat-sources/*.json: gas, vitro, wood) for what actually differs by heat source: TIME to reach a boil from cold (estimatedPreheatSeconds) and how precisely a simmer can be held — explicitly NOT the boiling temperature itself, which stays ~100°C at sea level regardless (see that file's own doc comment for why conflating the two would be a real physics error, not just an oversimplification). A real, still-open gap: requiredTools above can't express 'exactly one of gas/vitro/wood is required' (AND-only semantics) — this parameter records which was used without the engine actually requiring one to be present.
metadata.retrySafeNote: retrySafe: true (data-level, no duplication) — but see shock.json's carryoverCookingNote: re-boiling something already at the desired doneness will overcook it, a real physical risk, not a data-model one.
metadata.toolCapabilityNote: requiredTools changed from ['pot'] to requiredToolCapabilities: ['isDeepVessel'] 2026-08-14 (action.ts's requiredToolCapabilities, engine.ts's matching applyAction check) — added directly in response to being asked whether a robot with only a pan (no pot) could still boil an egg. It couldn't, purely because of an id-vs-capability mismatch, not a real physical constraint: BOIL needs SOME vessel deep enough to submerge the egg, not the one entity literally named 'pot'. pot.json and saucepan.json both assert isDeepVessel: true; pan.json deliberately does not (see its own noIsDeepVesselNote) — a real frying pan genuinely can't hold enough water depth, so this is substitutability among vessels that actually work, not blanket permissiveness. Non-breaking: every existing recipe's availableTools already includes 'pot', which still satisfies the new capability check.
metadata.placementMethodNote: Added 2026-08-14, directly answering 'the robot has to try not to break the egg' — the shell-fragility/handling-care gap named as unmodeled in scripts/boil-egg-as-a-robot.ts's own step 3 and ROADMAP.md's 2026-08-14 entry. THREE genuinely different real moments/mechanisms cause a boiled egg's shell to crack, and this parameter closes exactly one of them, not all three — naming the other two rather than implying this closes the whole topic: (1) MECHANICAL IMPACT at entry — an egg dropped from height striking the pot bottom or another egg — is what this parameter actually records: 'dropped' (real risk, unmitigated), 'lowered_by_hand' (held at the water surface before releasing — reduces but doesn't eliminate impact), 'lowered_with_spoon' (egg rests on a slotted spoon/skimmer all the way to the water, the standard professional technique specifically because it removes impact entirely) — see REFERENCES.md. (2) THERMAL SHOCK at entry — see startMethodNote above, already modeled via startMethod: cold_start avoids it, boiling_start (what EGG_BOIL_DONENESS assumes) doesn't; a real, already-named, UNRESOLVED tension between doneness-timing precision and crack-avoidance that this repo doesn't pick a side on. (3) TURBULENCE during cooking, once the egg is already in — see simmer.json's whyPerTarget note (a rolling boil's agitation knocking eggs against the pot/each other is, per that note's own citation trail, the MORE common real-world cause of cracking than thermal shock alone) — SIMMER exists specifically as the mitigation for this one. Like every other categorical technique parameter in this vocabulary, informational only: no crack-probability simulation exists or is implied — engine.ts does not read this value, and building one would overstate the precision this repo actually has (same honesty limit fry.json's heatLevel/agitation notes state). A real, deliberately un-built escalation named rather than silently skipped: piercing the egg's air-cell end before cooking (a real, commonly-cited technique to relieve the internal pressure that can itself crack a shell during heating) — no PIERCE verb or shell-integrity mechanism exists anywhere in this repo; recorded here as a known, real, unmodeled technique, not invented as a new capability just to feel complete.

verification.description: Water at or near 100°C (a visible rolling boil) maintained for at least durationSeconds

hazards.note: Boiling water and rising steam — splash/scald risk
